subject: english-language
title: Word Class Detectives
welcome_lead: Practise spotting word classes in a single sentence.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on labelling word classes in context.
final_note: You can now label every word in a sentence by class.

walkthroughs.body_html: 'Run' can be a verb ('I run') or a noun ('a run'). Word class depends on function in the sentence.
In 'The dog bit the man', 'dog' is the subject (doer) and 'man' is the object (receiver).
In 'She quickly opened the small door', label: She (pronoun), quickly (adverb), opened (verb), the (determiner), small (adjective), door (noun).

Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
Meaning conveyed beyond what is literally said — generated when speakers obey or deliberately flout Grice's maxims. 'Some students passed' implicates 'not all', via the maxim of quantity.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between descriptive and prescriptive approaches to language?
options: Implicature is a kind of grammatical mistake.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
Descriptivists describe how language is actually used; prescriptivists rule on how language ought to be used — modern linguistics is descriptivist.
Descriptivists describe written language and prescriptivists describe spoken language.

mcqs.q: What is Skinner's behaviourist view of language acquisition?
options: Skinner believed in an innate grammar module.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
Children learn language through imitation and operant conditioning — they are reinforced for correct utterances and corrected for errors.
Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
